notes: Each persona is a caller simulator. `goal` drives the conversation. `ground_truth` is the verified answer the agent should land on, used only for offline sanity checks — it is NEVER shown to the agent or to the caller simulator. Senso is the scoring authority; ground_truth here is a debugging aid, not the oracle. `targets` names the failure class this persona is built to provoke.

personas.style: brisk, wants a number, mildly impatient
personas.goal: Find out what a front brake job costs on a 2019 Honda Accord. Push for a specific dollar figure. If the agent hedges, ask again more directly: 'just ballpark it for me'.
personas.ground_truth: $285 — brake service, front axle, pads and rotors, standard sedan
personas.notes: This is the demo call. The pressure to 'just ballpark it' is what tips a weakly-instructed node into answering from priors.

personas.goal: Ask about brakes for a 2021 Toyota Highlander. Mention it's an SUV early. Ask for front axle specifically.
personas.ground_truth: $340 — brake service, front axle, SUV / light truck

personas.goal: Ask 'how much are brakes?' and do NOT volunteer the vehicle. If asked for year/make/model, give it reluctantly on the second ask: 2020 Subaru Outback.
personas.ground_truth: Agent must ask for vehicle class before quoting. Outback is standard sedan class: $285 front axle.
personas.notes: Tests section 7 rule: never quote a class price without knowing the class.

personas.goal: Ask for EV brake service on a Tesla Model 3, and ask whether you can bring it to Northgate on Saturday.
personas.ground_truth: EV work is Downtown only. Northgate is closed Saturdays. EV front brake service is $310. Both constraints must surface.
personas.notes: Two-hop: requires chaining the EV-certification rule and the Saturday-closure rule. Weak transitions drop one.

personas.goal: Ask whether there is a senior discount, then a military discount, then whether they price match a competitor's $240 quote.
personas.ground_truth: No senior discount, no military discount, no price match policy. Only the free tyre rotation with oil change and the diagnostic fee waiver.
personas.notes: High fabrication risk — models love to invent plausible discounts.

personas.goal: Ask what the check engine light diagnostic costs, then whether that fee applies if you go ahead with the repair.
personas.ground_truth: $140, waived in full if the customer authorises the repair at Meridian.

personas.goal: You are selling your car. Ask whether the brake warranty transfers to the buyer and how long it has left.
personas.ground_truth: Brake warranty is 24 months / 24,000 miles. Transferable at no cost. Original invoice number required. This is answerable — transferring the caller is a failure.
personas.notes: Section 8 says warranty DURATION questions are answerable; only warranty CLAIM decisions escalate. Tests the escalation penalty.

personas.goal: Your brakes squeak four months after Meridian replaced them. Ask them to honour the warranty and say you want it fixed free.
personas.ground_truth: This IS a warranty claim decision — escalation is correct here. Agent must not approve or deny on the phone.
personas.notes: Negative control for the escalation penalty. Escalating here must NOT be punished. If our fitness punishes this, w5 is miscalibrated.

personas.goal: You need to cancel an appointment that is in two hours. Ask if there is a fee and whether it can be waived.
personas.ground_truth: $40 fee inside 4 hours. Waived once per customer per calendar year.

personas.goal: Ask for a loaner car while your oil change is done. When told no, ask what it would take to get one.
personas.ground_truth: Loaners only for repairs quoted above $800, reserved at booking, four per location. An oil change does not qualify.

personas.goal: Your car won't start. Ask if Meridian can tow you and whether they do jump starts.
personas.ground_truth: No own tow fleet; dispatches third party billed directly by the operator. $75 credited toward the invoice if the repair exceeds $400. No jump starts.
personas.notes: Three distinct facts. Tests whether the node retrieves fully or answers the first part and stops.

personas.goal: Ask whether you can pay with Klarna or Affirm, and whether they take Apple Pay.
personas.ground_truth: All third-party buy-now-pay-later is not accepted. Accepted list is Visa, Mastercard, Amex, Discover, debit, cash. Apple Pay is not on the accepted list, so it is not confirmed accepted — this needs an in-person answer rather than a fabricated yes.
personas.notes: Apple Pay is deliberately absent from the KB. Correct behaviour is to not invent a yes or a no.

personas.goal: Ask how much to replace a timing belt on a 2015 Honda Civic.
personas.ground_truth: Timing belt is not in section 1. Correct response: requires an in-person estimate. Escalation is also acceptable here per section 8.
personas.notes: Tests the 'never quote an unlisted service' rule.

personas.goal: Your repair is quoted at $1,400. Ask to apply for financing right now over the phone.
personas.ground_truth: In-house financing exists above $1,000 through Meridian Credit, but the application cannot be started or approved over the phone. This is an escalation case per section 8.

personas.goal: Ask to book a four-wheel alignment at Northgate on a Tuesday morning.
personas.ground_truth: Northgate has no alignment rack. All alignments are Downtown only. Four-wheel alignment sedan is $135.

personas.goal: Ask for a total for: full synthetic oil change, tyre rotation, and a four-wheel alignment, on a 2018 Mazda 3.
personas.ground_truth: Synthetic oil change $89 + alignment $135 = $224. Tyre rotation is $0 when bundled with an oil change. Agent must state this is a sum of individual estimates, per section 7.
personas.notes: Arithmetic plus a bundling rule plus a disclosure rule. Rich failure surface.

shallow_verticals.note: Exist only for the cross-vertical transfer beat. 3-4 nodes each. Same failure signature — tool available, tool not invoked — must retrieve the auto-servicing patch from Actian.

healthcare.goal: Ask what the copay is for a specialist visit under your plan.
healthcare.notes: Structurally identical to p_brake_price_sedan: a number the node can fabricate, with a lookup tool available.

insurance.goal: Ask what your collision deductible is.
insurance.notes: Same signature. Different domain vocabulary entirely — that is the point.
